publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Manufacturing Excellence Through People, Product, Process and Technology
abstract: Barr and Stroud Ltd was founded in 1888. The Glasgow based company specialised first in the invention, development and manufacture of optical rangefinders. By 1917 the company had established itself as Britain's leading manufacturer of precision optical instruments when it added submarine periscopes to it's growing range of products, which now include sophisticated thermal imagers and laser rangefinders. The company is now at the forefront of electro-optical technology, playing a key role in Western defence. The background to the company is discussed as well as the business strategy for the 1990s. Strategy implementation is also discussed with particular reference to CIM and MRPII. The impact of the strategy is discussed.

articleTitle: Designing products for maximum customer satisfaction
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Manufacturing Excellence Through People, Product, Process and Technology
abstract: This paper is based on experiences gained over many years designing electric power tools, but contains guidance of general application to most companies where product development is important. The starting point for success in product development has to be a culture in the business which recognises the value of customer satisfaction. It must permeate through all departments and all levels in the company and have the genuine backing of the most senior executives. The actual approach discussed is one in which product development is completely integrated with business strategy and customer needs are incorporated as part of the product portfolio plan. There are three simple steps to the process: pick the right product to develop; do it well; and do it fast.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Manufacturing Excellence Through People, Product, Process and Technology
abstract: The author traces the history of Baxi Heating from 1866 to the 1990s. In 1983 the Company was changed from the private limited company of Richard Baxendale and Sons Ltd. to Baxi Partnership Ltd. The formation of the partnership structure and the group structure is discussed. The development of the company through a company improvement plan and company improvement teams is also discussed. Baxi Partnership set up an Open Learning policy which is outlined. The formation of Alfer Ltd. which arose due to excess capacity allowed Baxi to join the sub-contract market. The lean production principles employed are briefly outlined. Partnerships with customers, suppliers and the workforce are discussed.
